Package com.jasonwjones.pbcs.api.v3.dataslices

Class DataSlice.HeaderDataRow

java.lang.Object
com.jasonwjones.pbcs.api.v3.dataslices.DataSlice.HeaderDataRow
Enclosing class:
DataSlice
public static class DataSlice.HeaderDataRow extends Object
Represents a single row of a DataSlice: the left-axis member headers for the row, along with the row's data and any supporting detail.

    • getSupportingDetail

      public List<DataSlice.SupportingDetailWrapper> getSupportingDetail()
      Gets the supporting detail for this row, if requested and returned by the export. Like getCellNotes(), the list is positional against getData(), with a null element for each cell that has no supporting detail.
      Returns:
      the supporting detail, may be null if not requested/returned

    • setSupportingDetail

      public void setSupportingDetail(List<DataSlice.SupportingDetailWrapper> supportingDetail)
      Sets the supporting detail for this row, for sending with an import. The list is positional against getData() and must be exactly as long; the server fails the whole request otherwise. For each cell:
      • a wrapper with lines replaces the cell's supporting detail, but only alongside a non-blank value in data; with a blank value the lines are silently ignored. The server stores the value as sent and does not check it against the lines, so the caller must send their total;
      • a wrapper with no lines deletes the cell's supporting detail, and a blank value then leaves the cell's value as it was;
      • a null element leaves the cell's supporting detail alone, provided its value is blank.

      Writing any non-blank value to a cell deletes its supporting detail unless new lines are sent with it, even when the value is unchanged and whether or not this list is set. Supporting detail on an upper-level member is rejected with the rest of the cell.

      Parameters:
      supportingDetail - the supporting detail, one (possibly null) wrapper per data cell

    • getCellNotes

      public List<List<DataSlice.CellNote>> getCellNotes()
      Gets the cell notes (shown as "comments" in the Planning UI) for this row. The list is positional against getData(): element i holds the notes for data cell i, and a cell may have several notes. An export only returns notes when it is made with ExportDataSlice.setExportPlanningData(boolean) set to true, and even then omits this list entirely for a row whose cells have no notes.
      Returns:
      the cell notes, may be null if not requested/returned

    • setCellNotes

      public void setCellNotes(List<List<DataSlice.CellNote>> cellNotes)
      Sets the cell notes for this row, for sending with an import. What the server does with them depends on ImportDataSlice.getCellNotesOption():
      • Overwrite replaces a cell's notes with the given list; an empty list deletes the cell's notes, and a null element leaves that cell's notes as they are.
      • Append adds the given notes to the cell's existing ones, duplicates included.
      • Skip ignores them.

      The list must be exactly as long as getData(); the server fails the whole request otherwise. Each noted cell still needs an entry in data, and a blank entry leaves the cell's value alone. The server silently drops notes it will not store, without rejecting the cell: notes on upper-level members and notes with empty contents.

      Parameters:
      cellNotes - the cell notes, one (possibly null or empty) list per data cell, or null to send none
